description: Chat destinations. NO WEBHOOK URLS LIVE HERE. Each channel names the environment variable that holds its URL; the value is supplied at send time from CI or the operator's shell and never enters this repository.

secret_handling.rule: A Google Chat incoming webhook URL is a bearer credential: anyone holding it can post to the space. Google's own documentation says not to put it in a public repository.
secret_handling.where_it_lives: A masked, protected CI variable, or the project's secret manager.
enforced_by: policies/secret-patterns.json SP-10 denies a URL with inline credentials being written
scripts/secret_scan.py runs over the whole tree in CI
secret_handling.if_leaked: Rotate the webhook in the Chat space. Deleting the file does not un-publish it.

transport.v1: Google Chat incoming webhook. One-way, outgoing only. Supports posting a message and replying into a thread by thread key.
transport.not_v1: Anything interactive. Receiving @mentions, commands or button clicks needs a real Google Chat app that handles interaction events, not an incoming webhook.
transport.never: Approval. A chat message must never become production authorization; that lives in GitLab. See policies/approval-authority.json.

engineering-announcements.purpose: Organization-level lifecycle milestones, plus the incident-level events the wider group must know about: a failed deployment, a resolved incident, a published RCA.

feature-delivery.purpose: One thread per feature, carrying its whole timeline.
feature-delivery.expected_volume: a handful per feature per day, threaded

qa.audience: QA and the owning development team

security.audience: Security chapter and the owning team
security.note: Findings are posted by severity and area, never with an exploitation path. A chat space is not an access-controlled vulnerability tracker.

releases.purpose: Release planning, approval, authorization, deployment, verification.

incidents.purpose: Active incidents only. Everything here expects a response now.
incidents.note: Keep this space quiet. A space that receives routine traffic stops being read at 03:00.

channel_admission.rule: A channel declares which event levels it accepts. Routing a lower level into a channel is what turns a space into noise, so it is a validation error rather than a judgement call at authoring time.
channel_admission.why_incidents_is_narrow: The incidents space accepts incident-level events only, plus RCA_COMPLETED because it closes the incident's own thread. A space that receives routine traffic stops being read at 03:00, and then it is worse than not having it.
channel_admission.why_announcements_takes_incidents: A failed deployment and a resolved incident are organizational facts, not just on-call ones. The narrow channel is 'incidents', which is where the response happens; announcements is where the organization finds out.
